verdict.rationale: Elicit documents several of its own batch capabilities. Extraction columns pull data across all papers in a table, systematic reviews apply automated screening and extraction to imported paper sets, newly uploaded papers can be tagged as a group, and Collections can launch reviews or extractions on grouped papers. The docs do not show general multi-select bulk actions (bulk edit, bulk delete, bulk re-tag) across existing library items, and nothing independent confirms the batch behavior at scale. missing for 10: documented multi-select bulk edit/delete/tag of existing library items, explicit limits and scale for batch operations, independent or hands-on corroboration of bulk workflows

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can perform bulk operations across many items at once

citations.quote: Create a column for each data point you'd like to extract from your papers.
This makes it much easier to import titles/abstracts from other tools like EndNote, Mendeley, or Rayyan to use with Elicit's automated screening and extraction.
When uploading PDFs, simply click the "Add tags" button to create a tag or add an existing one to your newly uploaded papers.
Collections help you group related research, arrange it the way you want, share it with colleagues, and quickly launch reviews or extractions.
